Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May implementing Law 10/2010; Law 10/2010, Article 4, on beneficial ownership; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership and approving its regulations. Companies must identify, obtain, maintain, and provide beneficial ownership information as required by law. The ordinary ownership indicator is direct or indirect ownership of more than 25% of capital or voting rights; control by other means and fallback identification of senior managing officials also apply.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish registered office must be a valid address in Spain where the company has its effective administration or principal place of business, subject to Companies Act requirements. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for registered-office and correspondence purposes if it is a genuine, authorized address and the provider permits the use; it does not establish operational substance or satisfy separate tax, banking, customs, safety, or sector-specific requirements. For bitumen and asphalt trading, maintain credible records of management, contracts, counterparties, inventory or logistics arrangements, and the location of any goods. A warehouse or hazardous-material handling activity may trigger separate permitting and safety requirements even though the stated wholesale activity has no general incorporation-stage statutory license.

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-up at subscription. No statutory escrow account is required; however, a bank certificate confirming the deposit of the capital amount must be attached to the notarial deed.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire service or competent OCA (Organismo de Control Autorizado), structural load certificate for racking/storage areas, workplace safety compliance under Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 486/1997, including signage, ventilation, first-aid provisions, and emergency evacuation plans.

Paid-in capital rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-up at subscription. No statutory escrow account is required; however, a bank certificate confirming the deposit of the capital amount must be attached to the notarial deed.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The Spanish legal system contains no foreign-exchange controls on current or capital account transactions because the euro is fully convertible and Spain is subject to the EU Treaty provisions on freedom of capital movement (Article 63 TFEU). Both current-account payments and capital-account flows require no previous authorisation from Spanish authorities. Profit remittance in the form of dividend distribution and shareholder loan repayments is likewise free from exchange-control approval, subject only to corporate and withholding tax obligations under the domestic Spanish Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax, as well as ordinary anti-money-laundering verification of beneficial ownership. Any external transaction exceeding the publicly notified threshold must be reported to the Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistics, but the reporting requirement in itself is not an authorisation and never restricts convertibility.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed holding or collection period for export receipts. Export proceeds in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency may be retained by the exporting Spanish SL in any bank account or converted at the exporter's own commercial discretion. The sole residual obligation is the declarative reporting to the Banco de España of external transactions aggregating over the de minimis threshold of €100,000 per calendar year, and the maintenance in the customs/tax file of underlying documentary support (export declarations, bill of lading, invoices and FX settlement statements) to evidence that the commercial operation is genuine.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the supervising framework of the European Central Bank and the Single Supervisory Mechanism; for foreign-exchange and capital-movement statistical reporting, the competent authority is the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business (Ministerio de Asuntos Económicos y Transformación Digital) with operational reporting channels to the Banco de España.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Conditional Medium. EU-authorized Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) that passport into Spain under the PSD2 regime, or EMIs holding a direct license from the Banco de España, are legally allowed to provide payment services, IBAN accounts, and SWIFT/SEPA transfers to a Spanish SL. For a wholesale bitumen and asphalt trading operation, such EMIs are viable only for smaller working-capital flows, payroll, and contingency liquidity, because most EMIs do not issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, impose low per-transaction turnover caps, and frequently decline commodity-related transactions from the Middle East or Latin America unless extensive KYC evidence is provided. Offshore or non-EEA digital EMIs without an EEA passport are legally blocked from operating payment accounts for Spanish-domiciled companies and should not be used for any part of the treasury architecture.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Ultimate beneficial owner resident in a foreign jurisdiction outside the EEA, especially in a jurisdiction with opacity or strict bank-secrecy laws

Root cause: Ultimate beneficial owner resident in a foreign jurisdiction outside the EEA, especially in a jurisdiction with opacity or strict bank-secrecy laws

Defense evidence: Apostilled registry certificate of the parent company and Spanish SL; notarised shareholder register showing the full chain to natural persons; sworn UBO declaration on official company letterhead; EU tax-residence certificate of the UBO; documentary explanation of commercial rationale for Spanish intermediary vehicle in bitumen trading.
Off-high sensing red flag from commodity trading with high-risk sanctioned-border states sourcing feedstocks from the Middle East or CIS countries

Root cause: Off-high sensing red flag from commodity trading with high-risk sanctioned-border states sourcing feedstocks from the Middle East or CIS countries

Defense evidence: Complete upstream KYC package on suppliers including country of origin, INCOTERMS, original bills of lading, surveyor certificates of quantity and quality, confirming that the bitumen is non-sanctioned asphalt grade; demonstrated compliance with EU Regulation 833/2014 on restrictive measures; sealed contract and tax invoice triangulation from source to Spanish warehouse.
Frequent cross-border wire activity with irregular timing, or rapid round-tripping through the trading account before actual inventory is acquired

Root cause: Frequent cross-border wire activity with irregular timing, or rapid round-tripping through the trading account before actual inventory is acquired

Defense evidence: Board-approved treasury policy limiting payment windows; open-order repurchase agreements or purchase/sale contract pairs; warehouse receipts from the Spanish bonded tank farm; a clean internal audit trail for each MT103 transfer showing invoice reference, cargo reference, and tax number; bank reference letter from the principal trade executing bank.
Power of attorney or legal representative acting under an excessively broad mandate, creating ambiguity around signature authority and beneficial ownership

Root cause: Power of attorney or legal representative acting under an excessively broad mandate, creating ambiguity around signature authority and beneficial ownership

Defense evidence: Limited, notarised power-of-attorney granted exclusively for the specific banking relationship; Spanish national identity card or passport of the attorney; certified copy of board minutes authorising the bank opening; contact details and a corporate phone number verified by Bloomberg/Reuters article media screening to confirm the executive actually manages the Spanish operation.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Recommended compliant wire routing for an inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital injection is a SWIFT MT103 from the parent or shareholder bank to the Spanish SL's operational EUR account at a tier-1 Spanish bank. The remittance must include the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) of the Spanish company, the NIF number, and a purpose-of-payment value code consistent with Spanish balance-of-payments declaration practice (typically 'Capital injection / equity contribution' or 'Shareholder loan'). Where the SL was just incorporated, the first injection may be directed to the notary-blocked capital account required by the Spanish Companies Law for the payment of subscribed capital. The bank will require the original notarised constitution deed, the NIF certificate, the founding shareholders' bank account statements to evidence origin of funds, and, where injection exceeds €100,000, the corresponding statistical declaration must be electronically lodged with the Banco de España. The beneficiary bank will perform an automated sanctions/PEP screening, verify the LEI and NIF against official registries, and may initiate a source-of-funds questionnaire for flows originating from offshore jurisdictions prior to crediting.Bitumen and asphalt trade settlements should be cleared through two principal rails monitored separately: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct telegraphic transfers for prepayments, final balance payments, and post-shipment settlements within the conventional EUR/USD instrument range; and (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit governed by ICC Uniform Customs and Practice UCP600, opening via SWIFT MT700 through a Spanish bank and advising/confirming the LC through a supplier-side bank in the source jurisdiction. For cargoes loaded on ISIC 4661 bitumen drummed/bagged operation, the LC documentary set must include the commercial invoice, full-set original negotiable bill of lading, a sworn quantity-quality surveyor certificate, generic penetration grade test report, certificate of origin, and a beneficiary bank statement of non-conformity with sanctions lists. SEPA/TARGET2 may be used for euro-denominated low-value domestic and EU intra-community disbursements; however, non-euro or high invoice pre-payment to North African or South American suppliers must exclusively use SWIFT with field 70 references matching a purchase order number and invoice number, and the payment instruction should include the VAT identification number of the Spanish buyer in order to satisfy the tax authority's electronic invoice matching controls.European-style deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/MAD as required for bilateral asphalt contracts) executed under ISDA and EMIR-cleared rules with Spanish counterparty banksNon-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-deliverable Latin American and North African currencies for hedging the notional USD settlement risk embedded in bitumen purchase contracts without requiring physical settlement in the local currencyCurrency swaps (FX swaps / cross-currency swaps) on EUR/USD to hedge principal and interest exposures of the foreign shareholder loan or to defer conversion of temporary USD liquidity surplusesPlain-vanilla FX call or put options with a rolling 3-6 month tenor for asymmetric downside protection on dollar-denominated bid/settlement buffersShort-term natural hedging via inter-company netting and multi-currency cash pools at the Spanish SL treasury level, with the residual structurally exposed amount hedged by rolling forwards.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Conditional Medium. EU-authorized Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) that passport into Spain under the PSD2 regime, or EMIs holding a direct license from the Banco de España, are legally allowed to provide payment services, IBAN accounts, and SWIFT/SEPA transfers to a Spanish SL. For a wholesale bitumen and asphalt trading operation, such EMIs are viable only for smaller working-capital flows, payroll, and contingency liquidity, because most EMIs do not issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, impose low per-transaction turnover caps, and frequently decline commodity-related transactions from the Middle East or Latin America unless extensive KYC evidence is provided. Offshore or non-EEA digital EMIs without an EEA passport are legally blocked from operating payment accounts for Spanish-domiciled companies and should not be used for any part of the treasury architecture.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may apply a 15% rate during the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Qualifying start-up companies may also benefit from a 15% rate under the Start-ups Law.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% domestic withholding on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply where statutory conditions are met, commonly including qualifying EU or EEA residence, a minimum 5% participation, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment to complete it, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse limitations. Spanish domestic participation-exemption rules generally do not by themselves eliminate non-resident dividend withholding.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200: within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202: generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; the electronic deadline is generally extended to 1 to 20 April, October, and December, subject to the Spanish Tax Agency calendar.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed from 1 to 20 April, October, and December. The amount is calculated either by reference to the prior year's tax liability or, where mandatory or elected, by reference to the current period's taxable base.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 aggregate annual value of controlled transactions with the same related person, measured at arm's length value, is the principal general threshold below which the standard related-party documentation obligation may not apply. The threshold does not override specific exclusions or documentation requirements for certain transactions, including transfers of real estate or businesses, transfers of shares or interests in specified entities, and transactions involving tax havens or equivalent high-risk jurisdictions. A Master File is generally relevant where the Spanish entity forms part of a multinational group and the applicable Spanish documentation rules are met; Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate general Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to those of certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless required under Spanish anti-abuse rules, the principal-purpose and beneficial-ownership concepts applicable under treaties and EU law, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, transfer-pricing rules, and the general anti-avoidance and simulated-transaction doctrines. A Spanish SL should maintain genuine local commercial activity, appropriate personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure where commercially required, decision-making evidence, inventory and logistics records, independent banking, and documented business reasons. A pure conduit, circular financing arrangement, artificial invoicing chain, or nominal director structure may be challenged.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent filing

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and collection surcharges. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period may constitute a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine from one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of two to six years.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto directors may incur civil liability for unpaid tax and penalties where statutory conditions are met, and criminal liability where they personally participate, authorize, or negligently facilitate the conduct. Courts may impose professional disqualification and asset measures. Travel restrictions can arise from criminal judicial orders, but are not an automatic consequence of ordinary tax debt.
VAT carousel, missing-trader, or customs fraud

Statutory sanction: Recovery of VAT, customs duties, interest, and administrative penalties; serious or aggravated VAT fraud may result in criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, disqualification, and seizure of assets.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly organize or approve fraudulent VAT or customs transactions may face joint civil recovery, criminal liability, precautionary asset freezes, and disqualification. Immigration or travel restrictions require a competent judicial or administrative order.
Transfer-pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: Primary tax adjustments, interest, documentation penalties, and tax-geared penalties. Failure to provide required documentation can attract fixed penalties commonly calculated by reference to the affected transaction or adjusted amount, subject to statutory caps and the applicable offense classification.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability for deliberate or grossly negligent tax damage and criminal exposure if the adjustment forms part of deliberate tax fraud. A signed intercompany agreement does not protect a director where the transaction is fictitious or economically unsupported.
Shell company, conduit, or beneficial-ownership abuse

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty or EU exemptions, withholding-tax reassessment, interest, anti-abuse penalties, beneficial-ownership challenges, and possible criminal consequences where concealment or fraud is intentional.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for fraudulent declarations, simulated transactions, unpaid withholding, and asset dissipation. Veil piercing is exceptional but may occur where the entity is used abusively, fraudulently, or without genuine separateness.
AML, sanctions, and suspicious-payment failures

Statutory sanction: Spanish AML breaches may be classified as minor, serious, or very serious and may attract substantial administrative fines, public reprimands, temporary management or activity restrictions, and director-specific sanctions. Sanctions breaches may result in asset freezes, administrative penalties, and criminal prosecution depending on conduct.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance officers may be personally sanctioned for failures of supervision, identification, recordkeeping, or reporting. Knowingly facilitating money laundering may result in imprisonment, fines, disqualification, confiscation, and judicial travel restrictions.
Undeclared permanent establishment or disguised employment

Statutory sanction: Corporate tax, VAT, payroll withholding, social-security, and employment reassessments, together with interest and applicable administrative penalties. Serious labor or social-security fraud may result in criminal liability.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur joint or subsidiary liability for payroll, social-security, and tax debts where statutory conditions are met, and personal criminal liability for deliberate evasion or fraudulent labor structures.
Improper profit distribution and unlawful capital maintenance

Statutory sanction: Repayment of unlawfully distributed amounts, director liability for losses, creditor claims, insolvency consequences, and potential criminal liability for insolvency-related offenses or asset concealment.

Director personal liability: Directors may be required to restore assets, indemnify the company and creditors, and bear insolvency liability. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment, fines, disqualification, and judicial precautionary measures.
Accounting, corporate-record, and filing failure

Statutory sanction: Accounting and Companies Registry penalties, tax penalties for unsupported deductions, estimated assessments, loss of evidentiary protection, and possible qualification of accounts or insolvency consequences.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for administrative sanctions, creditor losses, tax underpayments, and insolvency-related damages. Criminal liability may arise if accounting records are falsified or deliberately destroyed.
